title: Replace a Broken Tile
subtitle: Home Repair
_voice: Daniel. The school's voice, owner's choice 2026-09-24.

brand.name: Professor Adow TVET
brand.by: A short unit lecture from Professor Adow TVET

objectives: Name the tools and the protective equipment, and what each protects against.
Mask and drill the tile to the depth of the tile only.
Rake the grout from all four joints before anything is broken.
Chip the tile out from the centre outwards.
Clear the old adhesive back to a flat bed, bevel side down.
Dry-fit, and read a rocking tile as an uneven bed.
Space, cure, grout, finish and polish.

beats.say: One tile in this wall is broken. It is already ruined, and nothing you do to it can make it worse. The eight sound tiles around it are the job, and every decision from here is about them.

at.broken: One tile in this wall is broken

beats.say: Safety goggles, because a struck tile does not crumble, it splinters, and it splinters upwards. Thick gloves, because a freshly broken glazed edge cuts like glass, which is very nearly what it is.
Two strips of masking tape across the diagonals, forming an X. The tape stops the drill slipping on the glaze, and later it carries most of the broken tile away with it.

Now drill holes along both strips with a five millimetre masonry bit. Only as deep as the tile. Wrap a piece of tape around the bit as a depth stop, because behind the tile is wall, and in a kitchen or a bathroom there is often a pipe in it.

Before a single blow, rake the grout out of all four joints. Set grout ties the tile to the tiles beside it, and while that rim is there a crack has somewhere to travel. Take it out and the tile becomes an island.
The cold chisel starts in the middle, where the drilling has already weakened it, and works outwards to the tape. Start at an edge and you are working against the neighbour, not the wall.

Strike the chisel. Never lever it, because the only thing to lever against is the tile next door, and a tile is weak in bending. Peel the tape, lift the last pieces with the wood chisel, and the old adhesive is what is left.

Take the old adhesive back with the wood chisel held bevel side down, so the tool rides up out of the work rather than digging in behind the tile beside it. What you want is flat. Nothing after this sits right on a bed that is not.

Offer the new tile up before any adhesive is opened. If it rocks, that is the wall talking and not the tile: there is a high spot still on the bed. Go back to the chisel now, while it costs you a minute.

Spread adhesive on the back of the tile with the notched spreader, and use it sparingly. Too much and the tile stands proud of its neighbours, and you will feel that step every time you wipe the wall.

Press it home until every edge and corner is flush, clean the adhesive off the face, then put the spacers in and leave it. Twenty four hours, or whatever the container says. The adhesive holds the tile; nothing else does yet.

at.flush: every edge and corner is flush

beats.say: When it has cured, take the spacers out and grout the four joints, then run the plastic tool along them for an even line. Polish it off with a dry cloth, and if the job is right nobody can tell which tile it was.

So: protect yourself and the tiles around it. Release it by raking all four joints. Remove it from the centre outwards, striking and never levering. Replace it on a flat bed, sparingly, flush, and then wait. The repair you cannot find is the finished one.

at.replace: Replace it on a flat bed
